Rules with a reason.
Our school held a morning of activity lessons for new pupils. I helped show a boy called Ben around. He looked nervous when we entered the science room. There were tables with equipment, and a bright line was marked on the floor. The teacher explained that we must stay behind the line during her demonstration. We must not pick up equipment without being asked. Ben thought the rules meant we could not enjoy the lesson. I told him that the rules helped everyone see clearly and move safely. We put our bags below the table and opened our notebooks. The teacher showed how a paper butterfly moved when air passed over it. Ben wrote a question and asked it politely at the end. Afterwards, we went to the IT room. There, a different rule was important: we must use our own accounts and keep passwords private. I nearly forgot to save my work, but Ben reminded me. At lunchtime, we talked about the morning. He said the rules made more sense when he understood their reasons. I agreed. I had learned that helping a new pupil was more than pointing out rooms. It also meant explaining what to do and why.
